CAP-011.notes: The current UI polls Core; no SSE/live-stream claim. Browser authorization uses HttpOnly device-session cookies and a readable CSRF cookie, never browser storage bearer tokens. QR pairing includes only a non-authorizing challenge identifier; phone sessions remain pending until owner approval and verification-code confirmation. The service worker is network-only and does not cache Core API responses or authorize offline work. Core reports CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, UNKNOWN or DISABLED from its private Office health projection; this does not prove mobile-network reachability. Requests, Decision Inbox, the tabbed Campaign workspace, Runtime, Settings, Access & Devices, Agent Office and the automatic Issues kanban are implemented. Agent Office projects recorded participants only; its Visual Office tab is a deterministic isometric SVG/DOM floor over the same projection, with one avatar per distinct participant_id, role stations, identity-stable slots, keyboard selection and clamped pan/zoom. It adds no simulated activity, and PixiJS remains uninstalled under the recorded renderer decision. Fixture Chromium screenshots exercise the renderer only; real Core/Compose browser acceptance remains NOT_TESTED. The 2026-10-28 studio amendment adds room composition, lighting, furniture and deterministic per-participant avatar appearances, and renders STALE/FINAL/UNKNOWN participants standing rather than at a workstation; Owner visual approval, real Core/Compose browser acceptance and independent acceptance remain NOT_TESTED. Issues has an encrypted GitHub connection, one repository binding per Project, per-page ETag sync with credential-generation fencing and credential-wide backoff, stable issue identity and safe plain-text detail; default-off governed issue intake now has append-only policy revisions, explicit immutable repository/author/label/profile/path/R0/budget acknowledgement, manually selected finite batches, deterministic eligibility, a durable lease/retry queue and reconciliation into ordinary REVIEW_PLAN proposals; execution remains disabled (no Campaign start, provider call or PR write), and a real authorized GitHub read, browser acceptance and issue-to-Campaign execution remain NOT_TESTED. Board ordering and non-delivery issue editing remain later work; Core-led comment/close receipts and retry are implemented, while PR-open/merge hooks remain WP3 work and live GitHub writes remain NOT_TESTED. The Issues view is wired at /issues and component-tested; real browser acceptance remains pending. Unified intake now has a durable Project-scoped request, append-only pre-freeze operator messages, an explicit non-autonomous execution-policy grant, exact profile revision/plan-hash approval, and authoritative Lead withdrawal fencing. Assessment requires an authorized model gateway; no fixture fallback fabricates checks. A real Chromium journey now follows the ordinary intake path through Worker claim, exact candidate, independent verifier, semantic reviewer with model provenance, deterministic Quality Gate, changed files and Core-restart persistence using deterministic fixtures. Exact per-role routing is implemented: the frozen profile Lead route serves intake assessment, the frozen Semantic Reviewer route serves candidate review through candidate → Campaign → start evidence, and the implementer route remains the Campaign authorization route. A Codex App Server connection is executable for implementation but not one-shot assessment/review. Discovered-only model IDs depend on the current Core process discovery cache. Live provider inference, Compose acceptance for the intake path, aggregate cross-role token/cost accounting and independent acceptance remain unimplemented; these are displayed as explicit limits, not inferred state. The legacy Compose stack E2E passes. Factory Office chrome and owned user journeys are available in EN and ES with a persisted locale and 320 px layouts; machine identifiers, statuses, repository content and Core/evidence prose remain untranslated. Docs workspace/editing remains a later slice. Decision Inbox now exposes only Core-backed actions with exact identity guards: approval of a frozen intake plan requires the exact plan hash/profile revision and explicit confirmation; ambiguous model reservations can be released; Lead withdrawal and Campaign cancellation require a reason and confirmation; every mutating action re-reads /office/decisions and aborts when the item revision changed or disappeared. Informational events remain separate and never render action controls. Full-scope Campaign authorization is not posted from the Inbox. Real browser acceptance for the new Inbox actions remains pending. Project onboarding now covers authorized GitHub repository listing and import through the existing encrypted connection, approved-root local import, human Project identity, a Core-backed summary and evidence-based manifest discovery. GitHub App/OAuth installation onboarding is not implemented; fine-grained tokens do not report OAuth scopes, and Office states no installation-wide access. Discovery evidence is advisory and never grants capabilities or check authority. The supported rootless Compose CI also exercises the unified intake lifecycle end to end (request, assessment, exact approval, Worker candidate, verifier/reviewer receipts, Gate ACCEPTED and restart persistence) at implementation `056c502`; it is deterministic-fixture evidence and does not prove live inference, Compose browser acceptance or independent acceptance. The subscription route requires an exact Owner-confirmed, request-scoped subscription admission. Productivity caps are not enforced. A real browser run reached a frozen Lead plan, a governed Campaign and an independent reviewer receipt in this workspace; independent acceptance remains outstanding. The 2026-10-29 visual-polish slice adds semantic shell/content tokens, a deep-navy application rail/top bar, 40/44 px controls and a conversation-first Home with compact Project/profile selectors, one explicit Core-required governed-execution acknowledgement, and lightweight recent-work/decision/status surfaces. Fixture Chromium screenshots at 1440/834/390/320 (EN and ES) verify structure and no horizontal overflow only; they are not acceptance evidence. Product Owner visual acceptance and real Core/Compose browser acceptance remain outstanding, and other Office views keep their existing composition until their own slices. Funding enforcement follow-up (2026-10-29): Core and Worker subscription refusals now provide stable SUBSCRIPTION_FUNDING_BINDING_REQUIRED, SUBSCRIPTION_FUNDING_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED or SUBSCRIPTION_FUNDING_EVIDENCE_INVALID codes with safe error reasons through existing API error surfaces. Worker checks subscription eligibility before historical monetary prerequisites. No subscription dispatch or recovery action is enabled. Dedicated subscription UI, real Core/Compose browser acceptance and pre-Project request admission remain NOT_VERIFIED; a positive monetary envelope cannot substitute for verified subscription funding. Agent Office V3 source candidate a294a43f1c837b721f3b40f4cf217294255742cb adds the continuous studio renderer, stable identity-sorted avatar appearance assignment, a 200-participant regression, and staggered back/front workstation rows with perspective-scaled original vector figures. Chromium fixture captures at 1440, 834 and 390 px are recorded in docs/evidence/agent-office-isometric-v3-2026-10-29/; they do not prove live Core or inspector acceptance. Exact-SHA independent review and Product Owner visual approval remain pending; vector art remains below the approved reference fidelity. The normative shell, Home, Campaign pulse, Agent Office and responsive rules are defined by docs/product/office-ui-standard.md; fixture screenshots are labeled and are not live acceptance. ADR-0034 removes fixed Office model token/time/retry/subscription-cost caps: those values are telemetry, not productivity budgets; authority, egress binding, leases and the Quality Gate remain. WP10 implementer Chromium acceptance against an isolated real Core exercised the Director plan review (lane/artifacts/stack/architecture/docs/skills/DoD/OpenSpec, pending/approved/changes-requested/rejected, missing-artifact approval blocking, rationale validation, stale plan hash refusal), reviewer independence (five required roles and assigned principals, per-role PASS/CHANGES_REQUESTED/FAIL/missing receipts with evidence, frozen-plan assignment mismatch), and finding resolve/refute with evidence and an authenticated owner decision. The run used labelled test-support fixture rows and real Core HTTP/SQLite projections, not model inference. It found and fixed a real Core defect: refutation required an owner-decision status RESOLVED that the owner-decision schema cannot store, so the action was unreachable; Core now accepts only the authenticated owner's APPROVED decision. It also fixed cross-request review-notice leakage, a misleading FORMAL_SPEC-with-no-spec message and unresolved {order} copy. Screenshots and a 39-row matrix are in docs/evidence/wave12-office-acceptance-2026-11-10/. The final integration rerun at code candidate `97690f4` repeated the 39/39 matrix and regenerated the manifest and screenshots; docs-only commits followed. This is implementer self-test evidence; independent acceptance and owner visual approval remain pending. A refutation is accepted only for owner-decision matter `FINDING_REFUTATION` with selected option `APPROVE_REFUTATION`; an unrelated matter or option is rejected. The debug test-support trace-fault endpoint is restricted to the seeded retry request, bounded to one map entry and rejects unknown IDs. The 2026-11-10 vlog run exercised the Project detail summary after Gate acceptance: the accepted Campaign d61a09f9 is shown as Accepted, the Project repository and GitHub connection are Core-backed, the issue-sync panel reports `OK` with `No issue synchronization recorded`, and old Campaigns and pending decisions remain visible as historical state. The Project summary uses the Gate-effective Campaign status (`934eabf`). This is implementer browser evidence at 1440, not independent acceptance. WP2 issue-linked delivery now freezes selected issues with the request, exposes Core-derived READY/QUEUED/IN_PROGRESS/NEEDS_ATTENTION/IN_REVIEW/DONE state on the Issues board and Request/Campaign detail, and Core owns an idempotent GitHub comment/close receipt ledger plus an operator retry that cannot duplicate a marker. A Gate acceptance alone never closes an issue; only a recorded merge can complete a mapped issue, and partially resolved issues receive one deterministic comment and stay open. PR-open and merge delivery hooks are not invoked by WP2 and remain WP3 work. Read-only tokens are typed blocked before any write. Real authorized GitHub write acceptance, the WP3 PR-open/merge integration and owner visual acceptance remain NOT_TESTED. WP1 adds an agnostic environment compiler surface: Core discovers committed conventions from the exact base commit, records a typed EnvironmentPlan, asks the frozen Lead model route for a schema-bound decision, records the Lead model call identity and an exact-plan/risk review, enforces the license gate, and freezes an immutable EnvironmentSpec before Campaign authorization. The operator may only trigger or retry the Lead review; the operator/Owner cannot choose or forge the environment decision. Director, Request and Campaign views show detection evidence, plan identity, license inventory/blockers, builder status and truthful missing/blocked/frozen states. The environment builder image/runtime and real Nix/devenv build are WP1-B and remain NOT_TESTED; no live Nix build, browser acceptance or independent acceptance is claimed. Greenfield planning now makes one bounded Lead-route stack-selection model call against the deterministic option catalog when triage/detection are empty, records a validated MODEL stack decision, and may use a bounded untrusted EnvironmentProposal to fill missing toolchains/packages/commands without overriding explicit constraints or committed conventions. Model proposals cannot supply Nix files; Core generates them, and the builder independently verifies every selected package version/licence/source against the pinned nixpkgs attribute before freeze. Resolution also realises the actual closure, rejects unfree/denied/unknown transitive packages and verifies planned command executables in the devShell. The selected stack profile drives architecture, skill and Definition of Done artifacts. The Office environment panel needs no new control for this: it already renders the resulting plan toolchains/packages/commands and the typed blocked/validated/frozen states. Live calculator re-plan and independent browser acceptance remain NOT_TESTED. Explicit operator recompile actions create a new immutable plan/environment revision only while execution is unbound; the prior rows are preserved, the rationale and prior status/revision/spec hash are audited, and the new environment requires Lead review again. The actions are hidden when a Campaign or authored specification is bound.

CAP-049.name: Requests and Decision Inbox
CAP-049.job: Start and follow operator requests, including owner-granted R0 autopilot, with human-readable state, see authoritative Core work that needs a decision, and act only through explicit Core operations.
user_actions: start a request, follow its human-readable state and filter the request list by Project or state
send one additional operator message to a completed or cancelled request to start exactly one follow-up request in the same Project and profile, with a visible parent/child thread link
inspect decisions, blocked work, unresolved usage and recent events and deep-link each item to its exact Project, Campaign, request, candidate or runtime object
enable one autonomous R0 policy and subscription confirmation, then select that profile and let the Lead assess, freeze and start without per-request approval
approve an exact frozen intake plan only with its plan hash and profile revision, an explicit rationale and confirmation
resolve an AMBIGUOUS or UNKNOWN Core model call with an explicit operator reason
withdraw a frozen Lead request or cancel a Campaign with a reason and proportionate confirmation
open the exact request workspace, Campaign, Project or runtime object without exposing removed pages
cancel an autonomous request or Campaign through the authoritative Core boundary
inspect the bounded, redacted workflow trace for a request: replayed final state, per-step status, ordered event log and structured replay alerts
inspect duplicate-sequence, missing-transition, open-step, terminal, truncated and malformed trace alerts without rendering tokens, prompts or unknown payload values
see plan-review missing artifacts and participant-plan readiness before an exact intake approval and open the Director to complete the plan review
CAP-049.notes: Requests and decisions are operator-authenticated Core projections; the client does not synthesize state. Removed routes redirect to the closest current workspace, unknown routes return Home, and copied path URLs without a hash redirect for browser navigation. The request list and Decision Inbox filter by Project. A V2 profile whose auto_start policy enables R0 is an autopilot profile: the owner grants the autonomous policy and subscription confirmation once, then Core owns assessment, freeze and start for subsequent requests without per-request UI approval. Manual profiles keep the exact plan approval flow. The Inbox exposes exact-revision intake approval, model-call resolution, Lead withdrawal, Campaign cancellation and navigation; every action revalidates the current decision revision, requires proportionate confirmation and is disabled while Core is unreachable. Full-scope Campaign authorization is not posted from the Inbox. Autonomous Gate repair and provider-session termination remain outside the Inbox. A real Chromium run against Compose exercised the request list, Inbox, filters, deep links and the autonomous R0 path; see docs/evidence/office-autonomy-ux-2026-11-08/manifest.json and docs/evidence/autopilot-r0-2026-11-08/manifest.json. It is implementer evidence, not independent acceptance. No SSE or live-stream claim. WP11 adds an operator-authenticated GET /agentic/requests/{id}/trace read of the latest durable workflow run. It returns a bounded ReplayTrace, per-step rows, a redacted event log ordered by durable sequence, and structured alerts for duplicate sequences, gaps, open steps, terminal/non-terminal state, truncation, malformed rows and replay rejection. Payloads are redacted by Core; free-form step detail is not exposed. The Request workspace renders loading, empty, error/offline, alert, step and long event-log states. WP10 now exercises the trace in a real Chromium run against an isolated real Core with seeded workflow rows: loading, no-run empty, Core error plus retry, populated run facts, duplicate/gap/open/terminal/truncated/malformed alerts, step trace, ordered event log with redacted payloads, rejected replay state, and 1440/834/390/320 px EN/ES layouts. The duplicate-sequence projection is injected by the test-support endpoint because the durable event primary key cannot hold a duplicate sequence; it still runs through the real trace module. Compose acceptance and independent acceptance remain pending; this is implementer evidence only. WP11 review repair: allowlisted payload strings are retained only when they parse as canonical workflow/step/outcome enums, lowercase SHA-256, operational identifiers or numbers/booleans; free-form strings are hashed. Property names outside the canonical payload keys are replaced by a bounded hash label, event IDs must match canonical UUID / workflow-<uuid> / step-<uuid> formats, and the Office refuses invalid payload keys, values or identifier text again. Transition rows with JSON-looking invalid detail or missing/invalid from/to states raise MALFORMED_EVENT, and a rejected replay is shown as unknown rather than in progress. Step rows are bounded to the newest 500 with STEP_TRUNCATED and a visible step-truncation state. Intake approval is fail-closed: Core returns PLAN_ARTIFACTS_REQUIRED with the missing artifact list, PARTICIPANT_PLAN_REQUIRED when the recorded participant plan does not match the frozen reviewer roles, count and assignments, or PLAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED while the latest plan-review decision is pending or not approved. The Request workspace shows the blocker and links to the Director plan review; the Decision Inbox does not offer the approve action while readiness is incomplete. The 2026-11-10 vlog run exercised the ready path in real Chromium: the exact request `037165ad-bc3f-4b5e-b8bc-db9f59338f83` rendered the completed assessment, frozen plan, five-role participant plan and workflow trace at 1440/768/390 with no document or body horizontal overflow, no unnamed controls and one h1. The blocking missing-artifact, participant-plan-mismatch, stale-review and changes-requested states were not exercised in this browser run and remain NOT_TESTED. Intake follow-up now records one authenticated message on a COMPLETED or CANCELLED request and creates exactly one child request in the same Project and exact profile revision; the child has its own Action, Lead request, execution context, policy binding, assessment, plan/environment/spec freeze and Campaign, and never reuses the parent plan, candidate or Campaign. A successful Factory delivery merges the protected default branch into the Project config base with a versioned revision, so the follow-up plans from merged main. The Request workspace shows the parent and the created child with its state, explains that sending starts a follow-up, refuses a second fork and renders localized EN/ES attention/refusal when Core returns FOLLOW_UP_EXECUTION_POLICY_REQUIRED or FOLLOW_UP_POLICY_PRINCIPAL_MISMATCH, including that another principal's grant is never reused. Core tests cover the different-principal refusal and the base-advance evidence guards; Office component tests cover the copy and states. Real Chromium/Compose browser acceptance and independent acceptance remain NOT_TESTED.

inspect a GitHub pull request state, checks, diff and comments for the candidate
open a pull request from an exact GitHub head branch or see a typed blocked state
request review or post a comment through Core without exposing a token
merge only after explicit confirmation and a fresh PR/check read; no auto-merge

follow a selected WorkUnit to its exact Run, Attempt, participant session, candidate, receipts and Gate
CAP-050.notes: Campaign authorization, Run state, Attempt state and Gate outcome are displayed separately. The Campaign and Request views consume the camelCase V2 `CampaignAuthorizationRecord`: schema version, risk/execution mode, route, authorized paths/tools, `policy.operations`, `policy.progress` and `monetaryEnvelopeId`. Historical V1 caps are optional `legacy` evidence only; missing/empty arrays never crash the Budget & usage tab. The WorkGraph now includes a deterministic dependency layout, keyboard selection and a WorkUnit inspector while preserving the authoritative table. Graph presentation states are explicitly derived from recorded task status and dependencies; malformed data is surfaced, not repaired. Candidate diffs are bounded Core projections from the frozen base to the exact candidate commit/tree: changed-file status, additions/deletions, unified patches, binary/large/non-file omissions, file/patch/byte caps and exact candidate/Gate identity. GitHub pull request reads and actions use the encrypted Core connection; tokens stay server-side. Merge requires explicit confirmation and a fresh PR/check read, never bypasses GitHub branch protection and is never automatic. Real GitHub execution is NOT_TESTED until performed. Participant, tool-event and visual Office projections are provided by Agent Office. The Campaign pulse derives the Lead completion/blocking status from the Gate and Campaign state rather than the raw Lead request state, so an accepted Campaign cannot display a running Lead. The 2026-11-10 vlog Campaign `d61a09f9-1564-4625-bb74-8e4a0ceded19` exercised the real Campaign detail: candidate `be5eb14f`, one verifier plus five reviewer PASS receipts, an initial `REPAIR_REQUIRED` on five informational findings, and a re-evaluated `ACCEPTED` Gate at `2026-11-10T16:51:03Z`. The Gate tab showed the two acceptance reasons and no operator attention signal at 1440/768/390 with no overflow or unnamed controls. The old repair-authorization banner was removed by `fc2b957`, included in code candidate `7960123`; the final 12:47 1440 px browser check against that candidate reported no repair-authorization banner (`has repair banner: false`) while retaining the Accepted Gate, candidate and reasons. The Campaign candidate and Gate surfaces now label the recorded `final_source` as Model final or Stagnation salvage; R1+ salvage also carries the typed `SALVAGE_HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED` hold. Candidate `be5eb14f` predates this field and is not claimed as salvage; migration `0075` assigns the safe `MODEL_FINAL` default and no historical row is rewritten. This is implementer browser evidence, not independent acceptance.

CAP-051.name: Runtime operational console
CAP-051.job: Inspect Core health, registered Workers, provider sessions, model-call usage, reserved ceilings, cleanup, telemetry, MCP tool-gateway diagnostics and runtime policy without terminal inspection.
user_actions: inspect Core health and registered Worker records
filter provider sessions by state usage cleanup worker or route
inspect recent and unresolved model-call reservations with measured usage and reservation ceiling
release an AMBIGUOUS or UNKNOWN reservation with an explicit audited reason
inspect telemetry export and semantic-review policy
inspect the role-filtered MCP gateway catalog, read-only policy and durable recent call decisions
CAP-051.notes: Sampled measured spend covers usage-known sessions and the latest 200 model calls. Reserved ceiling uses unresolved model-call max cost plus open provider-turn max cost. Unmeasured session count is shown separately; session cost is not claimed as a held ceiling. Supervisor, nested Podman and broker state are not exposed by the current Core API and are shown as unavailable, never inferred. Reservation release is explicit; no automatic release exists. The MCP gateway panel is Core-backed and read-only: it shows the immutable role-filtered catalog and recent ALLOW/DENY audit rows, never MCP endpoints, tokens or raw arguments. A missing FACTORY_TOOL_GATEWAY_CONFIG renders an explicit disabled state; it is not inferred from an empty call list.

CAP-052.name: Provider and runtime Settings workspace
CAP-052.job: Configure Core-owned provider routes, credentials, models, limits and review policy while distinguishing configuration, connection testing and proven coding inference.
user_actions: select a discovered provider model from a searchable selector while keeping connection details in explicit advanced configuration
save or replace a provider credential without reading it back
revoke a credential after explicit consequence confirmation
set the default route and keep token cost and rate limits in explicit advanced configuration
discover the real provider model catalog without claiming coding inference
enable or disable semantic review policy and inspect configuration audit history
CAP-052.notes: Credentials are encrypted at rest and never returned to the browser. A saved route is not proof of access. A connection test and model discovery read provider metadata only and are not coding inference. `GET /settings/providers/{provider}/models` returns a typed catalog status (`AVAILABLE`, `ENDPOINT_UNSUPPORTED`, `CREDENTIAL_REJECTED`, `UNREACHABLE`, `INVALID_RESPONSE` or `UNSUPPORTED`) with source, catalog URL and observation time, a bounded model list, no proxy and no redirects. `opencode-go` reads its sibling `/inference/go/v1/models` catalog without sending the inference credential; a missing catalog is not a credential finding, and a 401/403 is only a signal for that catalog endpoint. Codex App Server discovery is `UNSUPPORTED` by design. Discovery and the last-known snapshot are an in-memory Core cache and are not persisted. ChatGPT OAuth remains visibly blocked or not applicable. Provider revisions do not rewrite frozen Campaign bindings. Ordinary provider configuration uses a searchable model selector; base URL, manual model IDs, token/cost/rate limits and connection details are explicit advanced controls. Home and Execution Profiles no longer require turn, attempt, session, token, cost or deadline controls; Core V2 technical operation limits remain enforceable.

CAP-054.job: Enroll a browser without a permanent API token, maintain independent device sessions, pair a phone with owner approval, and inspect optional private Tailscale access.

inspect local and optional private remote access state
create a short-lived QR pairing challenge with a non-authorizing public identifier

cancel an unclaimed or approved-awaiting-pickup challenge
revoke a single device, sign out the current device, or revoke all sessions

CAP-054.notes: Session cookie material is HttpOnly. CSRF uses the dedicated readable SameSite cookie. Pairing challenge IDs do not grant authority and are stripped from browser history before phone requests. The phone receives a separate hashed poll capability, and Core creates a session only after the authenticated owner submits the matching code. The PWA service worker uses network-only requests; no offline authorization or sensitive-response caching is claimed. Access & Devices marks the current device, supports per-device and all-device revocation, shows bounded security activity, and cancels challenges explicitly. Tailscale status reports the configured private Office endpoint as CONFIGURED; the socket-isolated topology gives Core no health-probe path, so the UI does not claim live connectivity. Author-run deterministic and real Chromium pairing evidence passed at implementation 9afbb6f; mobile-data Tailscale access, independent review and Product Owner approval remain pending.

CAP-055.name: Provider-agnostic reviewer selection and bounded autonomy
CAP-055.job: Select a provider/model for the semantic reviewer, inspect canonical finding points and rationale, see deterministic repair authorization, and configure the outer autonomy budgets for R0/R1 while R2/R3 remain human-only.
user_actions: select any configured provider/model for the Semantic Reviewer role
distinguish chat-completions review from native adapter review
enable or disable bounded autonomy and set R0/R1 point and cycle budgets
inspect finding severity, canonical points, rationale and evidence references
inspect the deterministic repair authorization and its human-stop reason
CAP-055.notes: The frozen Execution Profile route is authoritative; Office does not invent a fallback provider. Findings are advisory model output, but Core recomputes canonical points, critical-zero, risk budgets and independence before recording a repair decision. R2/R3, critical findings, unknown risk and exhausted budgets are human stops. Autonomy is default-off and preserves historical policy hashes. The repair authorization is evidence, not an automatic attempt or delivery authority.

CAP-056.name: Owner-granted autonomous R0 intake
CAP-056.job: Enable one bounded R0 autopilot policy, then send an objective and let the Lead assess, freeze and start while watching truthful state and retaining cancellation authority.
user_actions: select an R0 autopilot profile and see that the Lead will assess, freeze and start without per-request approval
grant the exact autonomous policy and subscription confirmation once for a Project/profile revision
send an objective in AUTONOMOUS mode and follow assessment, execution and Gate state
cancel the request through the authoritative Core boundary
CAP-056.notes: A V2 execution profile whose auto_start policy includes R0 becomes an autopilot profile in Home. The owner grants the autonomous policy and subscription confirmation once; Core then creates the request-scoped subscription admission and runs assessment, plan freeze and StartAuthority::Autonomous. The runner is idempotent, resumes unfinished autonomous requests after restart and records a truthful Blocked state on failure. Manual profiles keep the existing assessment and exact plan approval flow. Autonomous repair, delivery and R1+ remain operator-only. The live run is implementer evidence, not independent acceptance; no SSE or live-stream claim.

CAP-060.name: Planner and Spec Manager
CAP-060.job: Compile a validated WorkGraph and author/freeze a formal specification with deterministic requirement, assertion and check identities.

author a formal specification draft for a FORMAL_SPEC request
freeze the exact draft revision by its preview digest

inspect whether the frozen reviewer plan is fully staffed before approving the plan
retry a failed model call or reload after a conflict
CAP-060.notes: The Planner and Spec Manager are bounded Lead-route model calls with distinct purpose and typed schemas. Core validates the graph and compiles the frozen identities deterministically. Planning is lane-routed and every lane requires a plan review; Core auto-approves only within the frozen policy and otherwise requires an authenticated owner decision. Plan approval fails closed until every lane artifact exists and the recorded participant plan binds exactly the frozen reviewer count, roles, assignments and WorkGraph. Planning artifacts are exact revisions bound to a SHA-256. Reviewer findings are durable dispositions and an OPEN finding blocks the Gate even when the reviewer receipt passed. A frozen specification is immutable; authoring creates a new revision. Wave 12 integration adds the supervisor/verifier/provider runtime-broker owner tokens, the six-reviewer fleet, the skill-pack refresh scheduler (source availability is separate from content review), the profile-gated OpenSpec validation job, and brokered dependency acquisition with an internal allowlisted egress proxy. Dependency acquisition is dispatched after provider writes and before offline checks; it is not visible as a new Office action. The 2026-11-10 vlog run exercised the ready planning path in real Chromium: one Planner WorkGraph, 13 FormalSpec design units, nine participant assignments, five required reviewer roles, one specification revision/freeze and an exact intake approval at 1440/768/390. The blocking plan-review states, finding resolve/refute controls, Skills refresh and trace surfaces were not exercised in this browser run and remain NOT_TESTED. Explicit operator recompile actions create a new immutable plan/environment revision only while execution is unbound; the prior rows are preserved, the rationale and prior status/revision/spec hash are audited, and the new environment requires Lead review again. The actions are hidden when a Campaign or authored specification is bound.

CAP-026.name: Risk-tiered delivery and auto-merge

CAP-026.notes: Core remains the only delivery authority. Gate ACCEPTED is necessary but never sufficient. R0 auto-merge requires an enabled RISK_TIERED policy; R1 adds explicit opt-in, a current Owner Charter delivery grant and a post-merge check; R2/R3/unknown are manual. Every R1 merge, including owner-confirmed manual delivery, runs the post-merge check. A blocked attempt cannot reuse its PR for a different base; the change is a typed BASE_MISMATCH. Missing or invalid R0 salvage evidence is shown as a blocker and disables delivery. The durable attempt is reserved before GitHub effects; concurrent different-base requests cannot both push/open a PR or call the issue hook.
